passage: Thursday night. First deadline missed today: the circuit board isn't wired. Feeling flat. Instead of blaming anyone, at lunch I sat with Divyansh and the others and asked why. Honest answers: I gave the wiring one afternoon and it needs three. The report looked small but takes an evening. We all guessed low for the hard parts and high for the easy ones. New plan: wiring gets three afternoons, Divyansh moves from decoration to help with wiring, the report gets two evenings shared between us. The teacher agreed to move the deadline by four days. Still tired, but not panicky. Small win: nobody was blamed, and everybody knows their share. - Sabina

qa.a: The wiring now gets three afternoons.

qa.q: How does Sabina feel at the end of the diary entry?
qa.a: Sabina feels tired but calmer and not panicky, and pleased that nobody was blamed.

qa.q: What could the team do to avoid missing the next deadline, and why?
qa.a: They could estimate the hard parts first and add extra time for them, because the missed deadline came from guessing low on the difficult tasks.

qa.q: How might Divyansh feel about moving from decoration to wiring?
qa.a: Divyansh may feel a mix of challenge and importance, since the harder job matters more to the deadline.

grounding: When the first deadline is missed, the team looks at why, finds tasks were underestimated, and redistributes work with more time allowed for the harder parts.

subtype: Approach: reflecting and reallocating after a missed milestone [Revision]
passage:
In the government school at Kalwa village, the Class 10 science club had promised a biogas model for the block-level fair. The first milestone, a working digester, was due on the fifteenth. The fifteenth came and went.

Nazia, the club leader, gathered the four others under the neem tree after the prayer. "No blaming," she said. "What took longer than we thought?"

Rukmini spoke up. "Finding a sealed drum. Took eight days. We planned two." Another boy said collecting cow dung from his uncle's farm was quick. The painting of the display board was already done.

Nazia wrote on a slate. "So the drum and the pipes are the hard part. Everything else we overestimated." She moved two members from the display to the pipes and pushed the fair rehearsal back by five days.

The digester bubbled for the first time a week later. Rukmini laughed out loud.

qa.q: Where did the club meet after the prayer?
qa.a: They met under the neem tree after the prayer.

qa.q: What does Rukmini's laugh when the digester bubbled suggest?
qa.a: It suggests delight and relief, after the stress of the missed milestone and the eight-day search for a drum.

qa.q: What else could Nazia do to prevent the next milestone slipping?
qa.a: She could set a short weekly check under the neem tree, so a slow task like the drum is spotted in days, not weeks.

qa.q: How might the members moved from the display to the pipes feel about the change?
qa.a: They may feel more useful, since the display was already done and their help went to the part that was really behind.

grounding: Shows a team reviewing why a first deadline was missed, finding tasks underestimated and shifting people and time to the harder parts.
